note: Best-effort technical mapping of MITRE ATT&CK techniques to control failures and compliance obligations. This is NOT legal advice and NOT a compliance determination. Whether an obligation is actually triggered depends on what data was involved, which regulators you answer to, and a materiality/risk assessment only your legal counsel can make. Every notification clock below starts on a legal determination (awareness, discovery, materiality) that counsel makes, not on the timestamp of a forensic finding. Confirm every row with counsel or your auditor before acting on it.

frameworkVersions.HIPAA: 45 CFR Parts 160/164 (Security Rule + Breach Notification Rule)
frameworkVersions.SEC: 17 CFR (Reg S-K Item 106, Form 8-K Item 1.05, Reg S-P 248.30, Exchange Act Rule 17a-4)

T1566.001.title: Literacy Training and Awareness
T1566.001.obligation: Workforce security-awareness training must cover recognizing and reporting spearphishing. A successful phishing-borne intrusion is evidence to review against this control.

T1566.001.title: System Monitoring
T1566.001.obligation: Inbound email must be monitored for malicious attachments and links, with alerting on detection.

T1566.001.title: Anti-phishing mechanisms protect users against phishing attacks
T1566.001.obligation: Processes and automated mechanisms must be in place to detect and protect personnel against phishing attacks.

T1566.001.title: Security awareness training is provided to all personnel
T1566.001.obligation: Personnel must receive security awareness training covering threats such as phishing, and acknowledge the security policy and procedures.

T1566.001.title: Security reminders
T1566.001.obligation: The security awareness and training program must include periodic security updates covering phishing.

T1566.001.title: Security of processing
T1566.001.obligation: Appropriate technical and organisational measures must protect the confidentiality of personal data reachable through compromised mailboxes.

T1566.001.title: Safeguard rule
T1566.001.obligation: Written policies and procedures must be reasonably designed to protect customer records and information against phishing-borne unauthorized access.

T1566.001.title: Information security awareness, education and training
T1566.001.obligation: Personnel must receive awareness training appropriate to their role, including current threats such as phishing.

T1059.001.title: Malicious Code Protection
T1059.001.obligation: Malicious code protection must detect and contain script-based execution, including PowerShell used to stage or run payloads.

T1059.001.title: Event Logging
T1059.001.obligation: PowerShell script-block logging (EID 4104) and module/command logging (EID 4103) must be among the events selected for logging.

T1059.001.title: Access to system components and data is appropriately defined and assigned
T1059.001.obligation: Access must be assigned based on least privilege, restricting who can run administrative scripting on in-scope systems.

T1059.001.title: Audit controls
T1059.001.obligation: Audit controls must record script-driven activity on systems containing ePHI.

T1059.001.title: Security of processing
T1059.001.obligation: Measures must detect and limit unauthorised automated processing of personal data via unapproved scripting.

T1059.001.title: Safeguard rule
T1059.001.obligation: Safeguards must address script-based access to, and extraction of, customer records and information.

T1059.001.title: Use of privileged utility programs
T1059.001.obligation: Use of utility programs capable of overriding system controls must be restricted and tightly monitored.

T1003.001.title: Access Enforcement
T1003.001.obligation: Access enforcement must prevent unauthorized processes from reading LSASS memory.

T1003.001.title: Authenticator Management
T1003.001.obligation: Authenticators exposed by a credential dump must be treated as compromised and rotated.

T1003.001.title: System Monitoring
T1003.001.obligation: LSASS access by non-system processes must be detected and alerted on.

T1003.001.title: Access to system components and data is appropriately defined and assigned
T1003.001.obligation: Least-privilege assignment must prevent non-administrative accounts from reaching credential material in memory.

T1003.001.title: Person or entity authentication
T1003.001.obligation: Authentication controls protecting ePHI are undermined by dumped credentials; verify and rotate affected accounts.

T1003.001.title: Security of processing
T1003.001.obligation: Credentials that grant access to personal data must be protected against extraction, and rotated once exposed.

T1003.001.title: Customer notification
T1003.001.obligation: If dumped credentials gave unauthorized access to customer information, affected individuals must be notified.

notification.from: becoming aware that unauthorized access to or use of customer information has occurred or is reasonably likely to have occurred

T1003.001.title: Authentication information
T1003.001.obligation: Authentication information must be protected through its lifecycle, including against memory-resident extraction.

T1486.title: System Backup
T1486.obligation: Backups sufficient to recover encrypted systems must exist and be recoverable; encryption of primary data tests this control.

T1486.title: Incident Handling
T1486.obligation: Incident handling must be executed for the ransomware event, including isolation of affected systems.

T1486.title: Incident response plan exists and is ready to be activated
T1486.obligation: The incident response plan must be activated for a ransomware event affecting the cardholder data environment.

T1486.title: Data backup plan
T1486.obligation: Retrievable exact copies of ePHI must exist to recover from encryption.

T1486.title: Breach notification to individuals
T1486.obligation: If the ransomware event is a breach of unsecured PHI, affected individuals must be notified.

T1486.title: Notification of a personal data breach to the supervisory authority
T1486.obligation: A ransomware event affecting personal data is a breach of availability and must be notified to the supervisory authority unless unlikely to result in risk.

notification.from: becoming aware of the personal data breach

T1486.title: Material Cybersecurity Incidents
T1486.obligation: A registrant must report a cybersecurity incident determined to be material on a current report.

notification.from: determination that the incident is material (Form 8-K General Instruction B.1)

T1486.title: Information backup
T1486.obligation: Backup copies must be maintained and regularly tested against an agreed recovery objective.

T1021.002.title: Remote Access
T1021.002.obligation: Remote access, including SMB/admin-share sessions, must be authorized, monitored, and controlled.

T1021.002.title: Boundary Protection
T1021.002.obligation: SMB must be restricted at managed interfaces rather than reachable laterally by default.

T1021.002.title: Inbound traffic to the CDE is restricted
T1021.002.obligation: Inbound traffic to the cardholder data environment must be limited to what is necessary; all other traffic denied.

T1021.002.title: Transmission security
T1021.002.obligation: Technical measures must guard ePHI transmitted over the network, including administrative-share access.

T1021.002.title: Security of processing
T1021.002.obligation: Personal data in transit must be protected and administrative-share access restricted.

T1021.002.title: Safeguard rule
T1021.002.obligation: Safeguards must address lateral access to systems holding customer records and information.

T1021.002.title: Networks security
T1021.002.obligation: Networks and network devices must be secured and managed to protect information in systems and applications.

T1071.001.title: Boundary Protection
T1071.001.obligation: Outbound web traffic must be monitored and filtered at managed interfaces to detect command-and-control channels.

T1071.001.title: System Monitoring
T1071.001.obligation: Anomalous HTTP beaconing to unknown destinations must be detected and alerted on.

T1071.001.title: Outbound traffic from the CDE is restricted
T1071.001.obligation: Outbound traffic from the cardholder data environment must be limited to what is necessary; all other traffic denied.

T1071.001.title: Protection from malicious software
T1071.001.obligation: Procedures must guard against malicious software communicating out from systems handling ePHI.

T1071.001.title: Security of processing
T1071.001.obligation: Measures must detect unauthorised disclosure of personal data over web channels.

T1071.001.title: Material Cybersecurity Incidents
T1071.001.obligation: If an established command-and-control channel makes the incident material, a current report is required.

notification.from: determination that the incident is material (Form 8-K General Instruction B.1)

T1071.001.title: Web filtering
T1071.001.obligation: Access to external websites must be managed to reduce exposure to malicious content and channels.

T1562.001.title: Least Functionality
T1562.001.obligation: Users must be prevented from disabling or tampering with required security tooling.

T1562.001.title: System Monitoring
T1562.001.obligation: Impairment or stoppage of security sensors must itself raise an alert.

T1562.001.title: Anti-malware mechanisms cannot be disabled or altered by users
T1562.001.obligation: Anti-malware mechanisms must not be disableable by users except when documented and authorized by management for a limited period.

T1562.001.title: Protection from malicious software
T1562.001.obligation: Malicious-software protections covering ePHI systems must remain effective and monitored.

T1562.001.title: Security of processing
T1562.001.obligation: The ongoing integrity and resilience of processing systems, including their protective controls, must be maintained.

T1562.001.title: Risk management and strategy
T1562.001.obligation: Disclosed processes for assessing and managing cybersecurity risk must reflect that protective controls can be disabled by an intruder.

T1562.001.title: Protection against malware
T1562.001.obligation: Malware protection must be implemented and supported by appropriate user awareness, including detection of tampering.

T1070.001.title: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
T1070.001.obligation: Audit records must be reviewed for gaps and tampering, with alerting on log clearing.

T1070.001.title: Protection of Audit Information
T1070.001.obligation: Audit information and logging tools must be protected from unauthorized modification and deletion.

T1070.001.title: Audit log files are protected to prevent modifications by individuals
T1070.001.obligation: Audit log files must be protected against modification; cleared logs indicate this control failed.

T1070.001.title: Audit controls
T1070.001.obligation: Records of activity on ePHI systems must be preserved; cleared logs undermine required audit controls.

T1070.001.title: Records of processing activities
T1070.001.obligation: Destruction of logs may impair the records and evidence needed to demonstrate lawful processing.

T1070.001.title: Preservation of records (electronic recordkeeping)
T1070.001.obligation: For broker-dealers, destruction of required electronic records may implicate books-and-records preservation obligations.

T1070.001.title: Logging
T1070.001.obligation: Logs must be produced, retained, and protected against tampering and unauthorised deletion.

T1048.002.title: Information Flow Enforcement
T1048.002.obligation: Information flows over DNS must be controlled and monitored to detect exfiltration.

T1048.002.title: System Monitoring
T1048.002.obligation: Anomalous DNS traffic consistent with tunneling must be detected and alerted on.

T1048.002.title: Outbound traffic from the CDE is restricted
T1048.002.obligation: Outbound DNS from the cardholder data environment must be restricted to authorized resolvers.

T1048.002.title: Breach notification to individuals
T1048.002.obligation: If exfiltrated data includes unsecured PHI, affected individuals must be notified.

T1048.002.title: Notification of a personal data breach to the supervisory authority
T1048.002.obligation: Exfiltration of personal data must be notified to the supervisory authority unless unlikely to result in risk.

notification.from: becoming aware of the personal data breach

T1048.002.title: Communication of a personal data breach to the data subject
T1048.002.obligation: Where the breach is likely to result in a high risk to individuals, they must be informed without undue delay.

T1048.002.title: Customer notification
T1048.002.obligation: If exfiltrated data includes customer information, affected individuals must be notified.

notification.from: becoming aware that unauthorized access to or use of customer information has occurred or is reasonably likely to have occurred

T1048.002.title: Data leakage prevention
T1048.002.obligation: Data leakage prevention measures must be applied to systems and networks that process sensitive information.

T1053.005.title: Least Functionality
T1053.005.obligation: Creation of scheduled tasks must be restricted to authorized roles, with alerting on suspicious registrations.

T1053.005.title: Event Logging
T1053.005.obligation: Scheduled-task creation, modification, and execution (EID 4698/4702) must be among the events selected for logging.

T1053.005.title: Access to system components and data is appropriately defined and assigned
T1053.005.obligation: Privileges to create scheduled tasks must be limited to authorized administrators.

T1053.005.title: Audit controls
T1053.005.obligation: Audit controls must record scheduled-task activity used to persist on ePHI systems.

T1053.005.title: Security of processing
T1053.005.obligation: Measures must detect unauthorised persistence granting continued access to personal data.

T1053.005.title: Safeguard rule
T1053.005.obligation: Safeguards must address attacker persistence on systems holding customer records and information.

T1053.005.title: Monitoring activities
T1053.005.obligation: Networks, systems, and applications must be monitored for anomalous behaviour such as unexpected scheduled tasks.
